places.name: ʿEin Feshkha · northern water installation
places.note: Northern enclosure: connected basins, stepped cells and drains. Proposed comparisons for entries 16 and 55; neither a hiding place nor a deposit is identified. Model position and bearing remain schematic.
places.source: Locality coordinate: Wikipedia, Ein Feshkha (31.7144, 35.4533), checked 5 November 2026; features: de Vaux 1959 pp. 230–233; Hirschfeld 2004 pp. 56–62, Fig. 20.

places.name: Phasaelis / Fasael · town water installations
places.note: The bath courtyard, large town reservoir and residence pool pair are separate installations. Upstream Fusail/Samsam reservoir is not placed at this town anchor. Comparisons for entries 3 and 55 remain conditional.
places.source: Town anchor: Pleiades 688003 (Phasaelis), 32.0275145, 35.443361, as reproduced in LACRIMALit; features: Hizmi 2016 pp. *151–*156, Figs. 10–16; Drive assessment 4–5 November 2026.

places.name: Cypros · numbered cisterns and water supply
places.note: Cisterns 1–2 and 3–4 are retained as separate pairs. Cistern 3 has reported dimensions and descending steps, but its individual footprint, stair bearing and entrance coordinate remain unknown.
places.source: Site anchor: PADIS archaeological project, Tell el-ʿAqaba (Cypros), 31°50′39.14″ N, 35°25′36.44″ E; features: Meshel–Amit 1979 pp. 71–72, 77; 2002 pp. 313–329; Drive reviews 3–5 November 2026.

1.evidence: Cypros adds a documented stair-descended cistern for comparison.
1.caution: Its east-facing stair, relation beneath a ruin and identification with Achor are not established.
1.sources: ; Meshel–Amit 1979 pp. 71–72, 77; Cypros numbering and cistern reviews 3–5 November 2026

3.evidence: At Fasael, a reported 10 × 10 m courtyard contains a 3.6 × 3.6 m stepped pool and nine reported surrounding column bases.
3.caution: The courtyard plan, column positions, required wall/opening relation and common early phase remain unestablished.
3.sources: ; Hizmi 2016 pp. *151–*156, Figs. 10–16; Fasael plan/identity review 5 November 2026

16.evidence: Feshkha adds observed basin-to-drain connections in a spring-fed installation.
16.caution: The retained reading, measurement origin and route destination remain unresolved; no 14- or 40-cubit route is plotted.
16.sources: ; de Vaux 1959 pp. 230–233; Hirschfeld 2004 pp. 56–62, Fig. 20; Feshkha/Fasael assessment 4 November 2026

17.evidence: Cypros has two separately numbered cistern pairs, 1–2 and 3–4.
17.caution: A pair alone does not establish the scroll’s two features, their midpoint, depth or location in Achor.
17.sources: ; Meshel–Amit 1979 pp. 71–72, 77; Cypros numbering and cistern reviews 3–5 November 2026

29.evidence: Cypros adds cistern and inlet comparisons from its water-system publications.
29.caution: The required north-side/four-side relation is unproved. A restored place-name cannot independently identify the site.
29.sources: ; Meshel–Amit 1979 pp. 71–72, 77; Cypros numbering and cistern reviews 3–5 November 2026

55.evidence: Feshkha has several interconnected basins; Fasael has a separate residence immersion/reserve-pool pair joined by a reported 5 cm pipe.
55.caution: Neither comparison identifies which pair or entrance the entry means, its depth datum, or the listed deposit.
55.sources: ; de Vaux 1959 pp. 230–233; Hirschfeld 2004 pp. 56–62, Fig. 20; Feshkha/Fasael assessment 4 November 2026; Hizmi 2016 pp. *151–*156, Figs. 10–16; Fasael plan/identity review 5 November 2026
